Delhi Protest: NSUI Workers Detained Outside Parliament Street Police Station
articles.description: Tensions escalated in Delhi after the National Students’ Union of India (NSUI), the Congress party’s student wing, alleged that police had failed to register FIRs concerning party workers injured during a protest. Several NSUI members staged a sit-in outside the Parliament Street Police Station, demanding that the cases be registered. Police personnel reportedly attempted to persuade the protesters to leave, but when they refused, several workers were taken into custody. NSUI members maintained that they would continue their protest until the FIRs were registered. The development followed a meeting between Rahul Gandhi and leaders of NSUI and the Indian Youth Congress, during which he reportedly encouraged young activists and students not to be afraid. Some NSUI workers were reportedly injured during the earlier demonstration and were receiving medical treatment. A Congress representative accused Delhi Police personnel of using violence against peaceful protesters and alleged that the police were acting under political pressure. The representative warned that the party would continue to challenge what it described as police excesses. These allegations have not been independently established in the report. The immediate dispute centres on the demand for FIR registration, the treatment of injured demonstrators and the police response to the sit-in.
